FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.97
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` claims sandboxed fix verification, but the optional test command is executed without rewriting file arguments into sandbox paths. In `evaluate_fix()`, the patched file is created under `tmpdir` via `_create_sandbox(...)`, then tests run as `_run_tool(test_cmd, cwd=tmpdir)`. If `test_cmd` contains explicit repo-relative or absolute paths—as the live caller in `immune_agents.py` does (`["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...]`)—pytest resolves against the original tree, not the patched sandbox copy. Evidence: only `cwd` is changed; command arguments are passed unchanged. This makes the core “does the proposed fix break anything?” capability test the real source tree, not the patched candidate.
FOLLOW: Downstream, fix evaluation can mark a fix SAFE/NEUTRAL even when sandbox tests would fail against the patched code, or HARMFUL for failures unrelated to the patch. In the immune pipeline, SAFE/NEUTRAL sets `finding.verified = True`, which activates the bug-closed gate and suppresses future findings as duplicates of a supposedly verified fix. That can silently close still-broken bugs and mislead human reviewers about end-to-end status.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — before running tests, rewrite any file/directory arguments in `test_cmd` that point into the source tree so they point to the corresponding paths under `tmpdir`, then execute the rewritten command.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66
DESCRIPTION: FIND — fix evaluation compares pre-fix diagnostics on the original file against post-fix diagnostics on the sandboxed file, but both are single-file tool runs. `_count_tool_issues(run_pyright, target_path)` and later `_count_tool_issues(run_pyright, patched_path)` invoke pyright/ruff/bandit on only one file. For pyright/mypy especially, diagnostics depend on package context and import graph; the module docstring for `_create_sandbox()` explicitly acknowledges that flat single-file analysis causes spurious import errors. The sandbox preserves full structure, but the tool counts still only inspect the patched file path, not the copied source set as a project-consistent run.
FOLLOW: A fix can change imports, symbols, or cross-file contracts and still appear SAFE because only local diagnostics are counted. Conversely, path/context differences between original single-file and sandbox single-file runs can produce meaningless deltas. Since SAFE/NEUTRAL drives `verified=True`, this can silently certify bad fixes and close bugs prematurely.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — compute both pre- and post-fix baselines by running each tool over the full mirrored source file set, using the original source set for baseline and the sandbox source set for post-fix, then compare counts attributable to the whole project run.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.78
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.49
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `run_pyright()` records line/column directly from pyright JSON start positions without converting from pyright’s 0-based coordinates. Code: `line=rng.get("line", 0)`, `column=rng.get("character", 0)`. Pyright’s `range.start.line` and `character` are 0-based in `--outputjson` output. The rest of the module and surrounding system use human line numbers conventionally as 1-based (`bandit` and parsed `mypy` diagnostics already are).
FOLLOW: Health scan locations are silently off by one for pyright findings. Any consumer surfacing these coordinates to reviewers or using them for follow-up lookup will mispoint diagnostics, degrading the health scan’s practical usefulness and potentially causing false “citation mismatch” reasoning elsewhere.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — add 1 to pyright `line` and `character` when constructing `ToolDiagnostic`, while preserving 0 only for missing/unknown coordinates.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.73
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — the advertised “defect detection” feature is not actually implemented as a distinct capability. The module header and focus state function 2 is “Defect detection — classify findings by defect category,” but there is no public function that takes findings or tool diagnostics and performs the promised defect-detection stage; only per-tool inline categorisers exist during scan parsing. No coordinator method exposes “defect detection” output separate from raw scan aggregation.
FOLLOW: This is a dead feature claim in a PoC module that the insect brain may rely on conceptually. Reviewers expecting a distinct defect-detection signal will not get one, and future callers have no API to invoke the advertised function 2. The module partially works, but one of its declared end-to-end features never fires.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — add a small public function that accepts collected `ToolDiagnostic` items and returns grouped diagnostics/counts by `DefectCategory`, and call it from `scan_health()` or `EndocrineLayer.run()` so function 2 exists as an actual emitted result.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.69
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.52
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `compute_pacing_signals()` uses `sorted(durations)[len(durations) // 2]` and the same pattern for response sizes, which is not the statistical median for even-length lists; it selects the upper middle element. With 4 models this inflates the baseline and suppresses slow-model / large-response detection. In this system there are 5 models today, but the code is generic and the topology/history includes model failure handling, so active model count can become even.
FOLLOW: After one model failure, pacing thresholds can become systematically too lax, delaying or suppressing pacing signals exactly when degraded operation makes them more valuable. This does not crash the PoC but can make convergence/pacing guidance silently less responsive.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — use `statistics.median()` for durations and response sizes instead of upper-middle indexing.
VERIFIED: TRUE
